items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions 'Jamie' (referred to as 'Jamie' in the prompt, 'Jimmy Woodye' in text, likely a typo or alias) only in a story told by the interviewee about Duke Ellington speaking to him. The interviewee does not describe a personal relationship with Jamie.

ctx.x: I said, 'Oh, my goodness.' So we come off the band-stand after the set. Jimmy Woodye come around the back. So Duke told him, he said, 'Say, Jamie,' he said, 'you know it's nice for you to sit out and enjoy the music.' He said, 'I know the band sounded good to you and it's nice for you to be able to sit out with the customers and enjoy the music.' He said, 'You know this is your job, though, and if I was you, I wouldn't embarrass myself like this,' and walked away.
